categoryNotes.zhs: 上公，指在三公之上。汉代多以此衔授予元老或重臣，其中以太傅最为常见。然上公实为荣衔，其政治影响多源于任者资历、声望及其所兼职。自武帝后，丞相多不设，至汉末魏晋动荡之际，丞相方复起，军事要职亦跻身上公之列。
categoryNotes.en: Superior Excellency referred to ranks above the Three Excellencies. In the Han dynasty, such titles were most often conferred upon senior statesmen or highly trusted ministers, with Grand Tutor being the most common. In practice, however, the Superior Excellency was an honorific rank, and its political influence depended largely on the holder's seniority, reputation, and any concurrent offices he held. After Emperor Wu's reign, the position of Chancellor was often not established. It was only in the late Han, amid the turbulence of the Wei-Jin transition, that the office was reinstated, with senior military posts also incorporated into the rank of Superior Excellency.

categoryNotes.zht: 西漢初設三公以分丞相之權。及至東漢，三公雖爵高祿厚，名義上分統九卿，然其議政之權已漸移尚書台，形成「雖置三公，而事歸臺閣」之局。故此際三公，頗類榮銜，其實權與影響力因人因時而異。魏晉時，尚書台多總攬機要，凡政策執行、官吏選任、文書上奏亦可越過三公，徑行處理。魏、吳以太尉、司徒、司空為三公；蜀國以大司馬﹑大將軍﹑司徒為三公。
categoryNotes.zhs: 西汉初设三公以分丞相之权。及至东汉，三公虽爵高禄厚，名义上分统九卿，然其议政之权已渐移尚书台，形成'虽置三公，而事归台阁'之局。故此际三公，颇类荣衔，其实权与影响力因人因时而异。魏晋时，尚书台多总揽机要，凡政策执行、官吏选任、文书上奏亦可越过三公，径行处理。魏、吴以太尉、司徒、司空为三公；蜀国以大司马﹑大将军﹑司徒为三公。
categoryNotes.en: In the early Western (Former) Han, the Three Excellencies were established in order to divide the powers of the Chancellor. By the Eastern (Later) Han, although the Three Excellencies held high rank and generous stipends and were nominally charged with overseeing the Nine Ministers, their authority in deliberating state affairs had gradually shifted to the Imperial Secretariats. This produced a situation described as 'though the Three Excellencies were maintained, affairs were handled by the Secretariats.' As a result, the Three Excellencies increasingly functioned as an honorary distinction, with actual power and influence varying depending on the individual and the political circumstances of the time.

During the Wei-Jin period, the Secretariat came to control most critical state matters; policy implementation, official appointments, and the submission of memorials could all be handled directly, sometimes bypassing the Three Excellencies altogether. Wei and Wu had Grand Commandant, Excellency over the Masses and Excellency of Works as the Three Excellencies; Shu had Grand Marshal, Grand General and Excellency over the Masses as the Three Excellencies.

notes.zht: 左校掌營搆木作採材等事，右校掌營土作瓦泥并燒石灰廁溷等事。故魏并左校于材官，而右校仍屬大匠
notes.zhs: 左校掌营搆木作采材等事，右校掌营土作瓦泥并烧石灰厕溷等事。故魏并左校于材官，而右校仍属大匠
notes.en: The Left Workshop was responsible for constructing wooden structures, procuring timber, and related tasks, while the Right Workshop was responsible for earthworks, tile-making, as well as lime-burning and latrines management. Therefore, during the Wei, the Left Workshop was merged under the Colonel of Construction, while the Right Workshop remained subordinate to the Court Architect
